1. Sumud Freedom Camp represents a new form of nonviolent political practice in which participants engage in relationship building and the development of new political programs through direct, face to face encounter.
Sumud Freedom Camp is a nonviolent initiative that has been successful in bringing people together across the political divides of Israel-Palestine.

the Sumud Camp experience is a non-violent, non-coercive, face-to-face encounter with the other that is based on the idea that we are responsible for each other, and that we are responsible to each other, in the sense that we are obligated to respond to each other's needs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the possibility of a new kind of praxis, a praxis based on the face to face relationship, and the possibility of a grass-roots politics based on such praxis, and the implications for justice and politics of such a praxis.
the question: What is the nature of the relationship that is necessary for justice?

the question of how to create the conditions for a new political order, one based on justice, in the midst of the ongoing Israeli occupation of Palestine, and how to do so in such a way as to be able to sustain it over time, even in the face of the ongoing occupation.

Levinas's philosophy, when put into practice, has a real and significant impact on the lives of individuals and communities.
Levinas's thought provides a philosophical foundation for the praxis of nonviolent resistance to oppression.
Sumud Freedom Camp, as a praxis, is a response to Levinasian ethics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sumud Camp is a nonviolent camp of Jewish, Palestinian and Israeli activists that is working to end Israeli apartheid and the occupation of Palestine.

Sumud camp is a nonviolent community of Jews and Palestinians, who are building a new relationship based on the face to face, in order to evolve a nonviolent political program that will enable the cohabitation of Jews and Palestinians in one state.
Sumud Freedom Camp is a space for the cultivation of a new political culture based on nonviolence and human dignity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the face to face is the only way forward for the Jewish people, and for all peoples, to live together in peace.

we can only begin to understand what it means to be human, what it means to live in community, and what it means to act justly when we are in the presence of other people, when we are in relationship.
the face to face is not an abstraction but a concrete practice.
